title: Token Clarity Pane — pricing profiles & attribution flows prototype
creator: Aisha Rahman
description: Design and prototype a compact, scan-friendly 'Token Clarity Pane' for the Redwood Console that surfaces token-level cost breakdowns, attribution signals, and exportable pricing profiles. The pane is intended for the per-route / per-model cost drilldown and should work for both high-cardinality accounts and low-volume trials. Focus on information density, role-aware visibility, and minimal API calls through progressive loading.
acceptance_criteria: A Figma prototype of Token Clarity Pane with desktop and responsive tablet states
Token rows show: token count, request/response split, mapped price SKU, effective unit price, and attribution tags
Ability to switch pricing profiles (e.g., default hosted, reserved/dedicated, custom enterprise SKU) and see recalculated totals in-view
CSV and JSON export flow that preserves attribution metadata and pricing profile applied
Design patterns documented for lazy-loading token detail and for summarizing high-volume token groups
Accessibility baseline: keyboard focus order, aria labels for toggles, color contrast for sparklines
comments: 2026-02-12 Aisha Rahman: Initial ticket created. Problem statement: PMs and finance teams need a way to validate per-prompt pricing implications quickly; current insights are too aggregated.
2026-02-18 Marco Liu: Wireframes v0 uploaded to Figma. Chose table+detail pane pattern to avoid modal clutter. Prototype includes sample pricing profile switcher.
2026-02-22 Sabrina Cole (PM): Requested inclusion of canary-aware pricing rows so we can preview cost impact of rollouts to a subset of traffic.
2026-02-26 Jonas Patel (Eng): Raised performance concern on fetching token-level logs for accounts with >100M tokens/day. Suggested server-side aggregation and sampling strategies.
2026-03-02 Design review notes: Use compact token sparklines (single-pixel line) and summarized attribution badges. Recommended collapse state for groups by prompt-set or user-id.
2026-03-05 Security review ask: Confirm that exported JSON strips PII and that audit logs reflect export events. Security: @Leah Kim to confirm KMS constraints for profiles.
decisions: Use a two-column layout: left side is a compact table of token groups; right side is an expanding detail panel for selected row
Implement pricing profile switch at the pane level (applies to all visible rows) with optimistic client-side recalculation and server verification
Adopt lazy-loading: fetch summary counts initially, load detailed token attribution when row is expanded or when user requests export
Export format: CSV for finance teams (flat rows) and JSON for engineering (nested attribution array converted to flat fields with keys) — ensure PII removal before export
